followups.problem: Explicit local=1 requests (Hive and Cockpit) are now uncached: every request runs a full board.snapshot. Previously they were coalesced and cached for 2 s under a bounded 128-key map.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Only token-holders can trigger this, so it is not a security issue. But a dashboard left polling a local-only view, or several concurrent local requests, each pay a full nine-project build, with no coalescing. That brings back the CPU cost the train removed, for that view only.
followups.fix: Coalesce concurrent local builds through a single pending promise, or keep one short-TTL local entry alongside the shared one. Either keeps memory bounded to two snapshots.

followups.problem: Cockpit responses are derived on every request from the shared entry.payload. The design relies on buildProjectCockpit and buildCommandCenterSnapshot never mutating their input; the diff does not show either function.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If either builder ever mutates the payload (deletes or normalizes fields, sorts arrays in place), the shared snapshot would be changed for all later Hive and Cockpit requests until the next rebuild. ETags would also drift without a data change.
followups.fix: Add a test that calls Cockpit for each id and then asserts the Hive body and ETag are byte-identical. Alternatively, deep-freeze entry.payload in development or test builds.

followups.problem: While builds keep failing after the TTL, every request starts a new background rebuild attempt, one at a time. The failure is swallowed by .catch(() => {}) with no log.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If the board stays broken, the server rebuilds back-to-back on every poll and serves stale data indefinitely. Nothing tells the operator, and the response shows no staleness.
followups.fix: Log the rebuild failure (error name or code only) and add a short retry backoff, e.g. 5 s, after a failed refresh.

followups.problem: The readRunStates stat/mtime cache was removed, so every caller now re-reads and re-parses every run state.json, up to the 5000-run limit.
followups.exploit_or_failure: The board snapshot path is fine behind the 60 s TTL. Any other per-poll or event-stream caller of readRunStates (e.g. the watch payload or delta paths) now pays full JSON parsing for every historical run on every call.
followups.fix: Confirm no other hot caller uses readRunStates. Otherwise restore a bounded (size and mtime) cache scoped to those callers.

followups.problem: combinedUsage is now always awaited, even when the transcript set is empty; the old explicit zero default for that case is gone.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If combinedUsage([]) does not return { todayListUsd: 0, allListUsd: 0 }, a board with no transcripts gets undefined or NaN machine orchestrator totals.
followups.fix: Restore the transcripts.size guard, or add a test for a board with no transcripts.

followups.problem: ledgerFromProject now always fills synthetic `${status}-${i}` rows next to real card ticket rows.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A real ticket id such as 'ready-3' could collide with a synthetic id in the Cockpit list. This is cosmetic only.
followups.fix: Use a prefix that cannot appear in a real ticket id for synthetic rows (e.g. '~ready-3').

summary: No blockers. Snapshot cache: there is one shared entry, built only with {local:false, redact:true}. Query strings and project ids never change the cache key or the build options. local=1 requests are computed separately, still with redact:true, and never written into the shared entry, so the shared cache cannot be poisoned and one project cannot leak into another. Cockpit is selected by id from the same payload. Rebuilds are single-flight through snapshotPending. Startup warm and cold requests share that one promise. A completed build replaces the entry atomically and is dropped if the server has closed. Stale requests return the old entry and validators immediately while at most one background refresh runs. A failed refresh keeps the stale entry, and the next request retries. Clock skew backwards (now < at) also triggers a refresh. Memory is bounded to the current entry plus at most one in-flight build. The response, header and ETag path at the caller is not touched in the diff, so CSP, nosniff, token/cookie checks and 304 handling still go through the existing code. Tests assert the 403 without a token, the CSP and nosniff headers, and 304s for both Hive and Cockpit. D-fix 27c matches the manifest exactly: two catches gained logging, with the same fall-through and best-effort cleanup. Only the fixed strings, error name and error code are logged; no paths, messages or cache contents. The three LEAVE catches are unchanged. watch-perf.parsePsTime is a strict regex covering seconds, m:ss.ss, h:mm:ss.ss and d-h:mm:ss.ss. redactUrl is unchanged and still covers logged URLs and error text. The version bump is consistent. Limits: I reviewed only the diff and the listed files, not the full watch-server request handler, buildProjectCockpit or combinedUsage, and I did not run the tests.
